title.narrative: WASH Flood response in the affected five counties, Aweil East, Fangak, Nasir, Mayendit, and Rukona counties, and cholera response in Rubkona county

description.narrative: South Sudan faces an intensifying humanitarian crisis, with approximately 9 million people, or three-quarters of the population requiring urgent humanitarian assistance. This dire humanitarian situation is driven by prolonged conflicts, worsening food insecurity, spillover effects of the Sudan crisis, severe economic downturn, and political instability. The crisis is further exacerbated by ongoing floods, cholera outbreaks, and a continuous influx of returnees from Sudan, straining already overstretched response capacities. The ongoing flooding and cholera outbreak will severely limit the capacity of humanitarian partners to adequately respond to the situation and provide the necessary support to affected communities.The project focuses on effectively responding to the WASH needs of the affected, targeting five counties of Mayendit, Rubkona, Nasir, Aweil East, and Fangak, which are among the priority 1 counties listed in the WASH Cluster severity classification. The counties are already experiencing more than in the previous years escalated flood incidents and, subsequently, massive displacement. The floods have significantly damaged WASH infrastructure and disrupted critical lifesaving services, including access to safe water and sanitation, deepening the vulnerability of the people living in these geographic locations. The floods present a heightened risk of outbreaks of waterborne and sanitation-related diseases as a mixture of fecal waste with flood waters is witnessed. Open defecation has worsened amidst the flooding of the already scarce and inadequate latrines in the project areas. Water supply sources such as boreholes and water yards have been flooded further reducing access to safe water.This project seeks to provide life-saving WASH interventions to 255,026 affected people (women - 71,407, Men - 61,206, Girls - 63,757, and boys - 58,656) in the 5 project locations. The project will be implemented in 2 phases: immediate-term – preparedness and response; and medium-term – recovery. In the immediate term, critical WASH supplies will be replenished to be accessible. The affected will be served with WASH NFIs including household water treatment chemicals distributed through nutrition sites (special attention to Severe Acute Malnutrition, and Moderate Acute Malnutrition families) and targeted distributions in schools and communities. A total of 127,513 people affected by flood and cholera will be reached with critical lifesaving WASH NFIs. Specific needs of women will be captured through deliberate and consistent efforts to engage them in menstrual hygiene management (MHM) by the distribution of dignity kits reaching out to 5,105 adolescents to meet this feminine-specific need. The medium term will focus on restoring the WASH services through the establishment of 6 surface water treatment systems (SWATs); construction of 8 new boreholes; repair and/or rehabilitation of 90 boreholes 5 Installation of solar water yards (SWYs), etc. 651 (women 391 and Men 260) people will be trained as Water Management Committee members to enable WASH services sustainably managed, properly maintained, and accessible to all members of the community, contributing to improved public health. In addition, 224 (women 90, and 134 men) people will be trained as Hand pump mechanics/WASH technicians for sustainable operation and management of the water systems/facilities. A total of 50 blocks with 196 stances of latrines will be constructed, and 24 blocks with 96 stances will be rehabilitated in the project areas. additionally, 159,974 people will be reached through indirect interventions such as hygiene messaging through the radio and awareness campaign. To enable interventions and supplies to reach beneficiaries with the required quality, UNICEF will undertake post-distribution monitoring (PDM).
